exposure: Fever in term pregnancy (low fever, high fever)
outcome: Maternal outcome (postoperative wound infection, postpartum hemorrhage, pneumonia, septicemia, jaundice, hypoglycemia, maternal mortality)

Fetal outcome (low birth weight, intrauterine growth retardation, preterm delivery, neonatal sepsis, perinatal mortality, neonatal seizures, poor APGAR score at birth, need for resuscitation, intra ventricular hemorrhage, periventricular leukomalacia, cerebral palsy, neonatal mortality)
cohort: The study included 70 febrile pregnant women of term gestation, predominantly aged 21-30 years, with 67% being primigravida, in a tertiary care hospital.
finding: There was a significant positive relationship between low fever, high fever, and maternal outcome, but a non-significant positive relationship between low fever, high fever, and fetal outcome, with UTI and Dengue being the common causes of fever.
mod_finding: 52% of the febrile pregnant women in the study cohort had a C Section delivery.
cross-section timing: The study focused on pregnant women experiencing fever during term gestation.
